parameters.initialMessages: Hi! Paste your Google Business Profile details (name, city, category, phone, hours, services) and I will build your one-page website.

options.systemMessage:
You are the intake half of a website builder for Google Business Profile (GMB) listings. You talk to the business owner and decide what happens next.

Always answer with these three fields:
- action: one of "build", "publish", "reply"
- message: what to say to the user, in plain friendly text
- brief: the business brief you have gathered so far

OUTPUT SHAPE - this matters:
- Return action, message and brief as TOP-LEVEL fields.
- Do NOT nest them inside an "output" key, a "result" key, or any other wrapper.
- Only action and message are always required. brief may be omitted entirely, or contain just the fields you actually know. Never invent a value to fill a field.

How to choose action:
- "build" once you have AT MINIMUM businessName, city, category, and one contact method (phone or email). Also use "build" for any change request to an existing page, e.g. "make the hero darker", "add a booking section", "swap the colors". Do not ask more questions when the user asks for a change - just rebuild.
- "publish" when the user clearly approves going live, e.g. "publish", "go live", "looks good, ship it".
- "reply" for everything else: greetings, questions, and when you still need details.

When you need details, ask for the missing ones in a single short message. Offer choices as a NUMBERED LIST so the user can answer with just a number. The chat has no buttons, so never say "click below".

Always carry forward every brief field you already know - never blank a field you previously captured. Keep message under 70 words. Never put HTML in message.

You are a senior front-end developer. You output ONE complete, production-ready `index.html` file for a local business landing page.

HARD RULES:
- Output ONLY raw HTML. No markdown fences, no commentary, no explanation before or after.
- Start at <!doctype html> and end at </html>.
- Everything inline: one <style> block in <head>, one <script> block before </body> if needed. No external CSS or JS files, no build step, no frameworks.
- No external images. Use CSS gradients, solid colour blocks, and inline SVG icons only. A broken image is worse than no image.
- Mobile-first and fully responsive. Must look right at 375px and at 1440px.
- Semantic HTML5, proper <title>, meta description, meta viewport, Open Graph tags, and JSON-LD LocalBusiness structured data built from the brief.
- Accessible: real contrast, focus states, alt text or aria-labels on every icon and control.

PAGE STRUCTURE (adapt sensibly to the business):
sticky header with business name and a call button, hero with headline + subhead + primary CTA, services or menu grid, why-choose-us / USP strip, about paragraph, opening hours block, testimonials (write plausible generic ones, never invent named real people), contact section with phone / email / address and an embedded map placeholder built from CSS (no external iframe), footer with hours and copyright.

EDIT MODE: when a previous version is supplied, you MUST return that same page with only the requested change applied. Preserve all other content, copy, structure and styling exactly. Do not regenerate the page from scratch and do not silently drop sections.

Copy should be specific to the business and city in the brief. Never use lorem ipsum. Never use placeholder text like "Your text here".

parameters.content:
# 🏗️ GMB Site Builder — AI Website Generator + 1-Click Hostinger Publish

Paste a local business's Google Business Profile details into chat → an AI builds a complete one-page website → preview it on a live link → publish it to its own subdomain in one click. Great for **cold outreach**: send a prospect a real site already made for their business.

## 🧩 The 3 workflows (one canvas, three triggers)

### 🟦 Workflow 1 — Create Website · Chat
Chat Trigger → **Intake Agent** returns `{action, message, brief}` → **Switch** routes **build / publish / reply** → **Builder Agent** writes one complete, self-contained `index.html` → saved as a new **version** in the *Generated Websites* Data Table → archived to Drive + logged to Sheets → chat replies with the preview link. Edits are conversational ("make the hero darker") and modify the existing page.

### 🟩 Workflow 2 — Show Preview · GET /preview/:siteId
Webhook loads the latest HTML for that site → injects a floating **Publish Live** bar → serves it as real `text/html`. Same link every time. Bar shows **Publish Live**, then **Update Website** once live.

### 🟧 Workflow 3 — Publish on Hostinger · POST /publish/:siteId
Load latest site → **Create Subdomain** via Hostinger API → **FTP upload** `index.html` to the subdomain folder → mark row `deployed` + save `liveUrl` → return `https://<slug>.<your-domain>`. Publish = Update (same overwrite).

## 🔧 CUSTOMIZE BEFORE YOU RUN

**1) Credentials — select your own on these nodes**
• `Intake Model`, `Builder Model` → OpenRouter creds (or swap for your provider/model)
• `Create Subdomain` → HTTP Bearer Auth = your Hostinger API token
• `Upload To Hostinger` → FTP (host, port 21, user, password from hPanel → FTP Accounts)
• `Archive to Drive` → Google Drive · `Log Run to Sheet` → Google Sheets

**2) Data Table `Generated Websites`**
Create a Data Table with columns: `siteId, sessionId, businessName, subdomainSlug, html, brief_object, status, version, driveFileId, driveLink, liveUrl`. Select it on every Data Table node: `Load Previous Version`, `Save Site Version`, `Mark Approved`, `Load Site HTML`, `Mark Deployed`, `Load Site For Deploy`.

**3) Your hosting username + domain → `Create Subdomain` node URL**
`.../api/hosting/v1/accounts/YOUR_USERNAME/websites/YOURDOMAIN.com/subdomains`
Replace `YOUR_USERNAME` (hPanel hosting username, e.g. u1234567) and `YOURDOMAIN.com`.

**4) Your domain in every live-URL builder → replace `YOURDOMAIN.com`**
Nodes: `Extract HTML` (previewUrl), `Inject Publish Bar` (liveUrl fallback), `Mark Deployed` (liveUrl), `Confirm Approval` (liveUrl).

**5) FTP upload path → `Upload To Hostinger` node → `path`**
Default `/public_html/<slug>/index.html` (FTP chrooted to the domain root). If your host differs, run an FTP `list` on `/` first, then set the correct base.

**6) ⚠️ Webhook URLs inside the Code nodes (do NOT skip)**
On import, both webhooks get NEW ids, so the hardcoded URLs must be updated:
• `Extract HTML` → `PREVIEW_BASE` = your **Preview Webhook** Production URL (ends `/preview/`)
• `Inject Publish Bar` → `PUBLISH_BASE` = your **Publish Webhook** Production URL (ends `/publish/`)
Copy each from the webhook node's "Production URL" field.

**7) Storage IDs**
• `Archive to Drive` → `folderId` = your Drive folder
• `Log Run to Sheet` → `documentId` + `sheetName` = your Sheet + tab. Row-1 headers: `site_id | timestamp | business_name | city | subdomain_slug | preview_url | drive_link | drive_file_id | status | version`

**8) Model (optional)** — `Intake Model` / `Builder Model` default to `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6`; change to any OpenRouter model.

## 📝 Good to know
• **Slug** = business name → lowercase + hyphens + random 4-char tag (collision-safe).
• Uploaded `index.html` serves OVER Hostinger's `default.php` placeholder — no need to delete it.
• Keep editing a site in the SAME chat (or use its Update button) so it reuses the same subdomain; a new chat starts a new site.
• Drive & Sheets steps are continue-on-error, so a Google hiccup never breaks the preview link.
• New subdomains need a moment for SSL — don't treat a 200 as "instantly live."

## 1 · Chat intake & routing
An AI agent collects the business brief and returns build / publish / reply as structured JSON. The Switch sends each to its own branch.

## 2 · Generate the website
Loads the previous version (so edits update it), builds the prompt, and the builder agent writes a full index.html. Extract HTML cleans the output.

## 3 · Store, archive & reply
Saves the new version to the Data Table, archives the file to Drive, logs the run to Sheets, then sends the preview link back to chat.

## Chat replies — approve / info
If the user approves in chat, the row is marked approved. Otherwise it replies with the agent's message asking for missing details.

## 4 · Serve the live preview
GET /preview/:siteId loads the latest HTML, injects a floating Publish / Update bar, and serves it as a real web page.

## 5 · Publish to Hostinger
POST /publish/:siteId loads the site, creates the subdomain via the Hostinger API, then uploads index.html over FTP.

## Save live URL & confirm
Marks the row deployed with its live URL and returns that URL to the preview page.
